question.text: A box contains <math><mn>9</mn></math> slips bearing numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1,</mn><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1,</mn><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3,</mn><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>. An experiment consists of drawing a slip from this box and replacing it back in the box after noting the number. This experiment is repeated <math><mn>9</mn></math> times. These <math><mn>9</mn></math> numbers are now chosen as elements of a <math><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>3</mn></math> matrix, then the probability that the matrix is skew symmetric is

solution.text:
Total cases =99
All diagonal elements are zero and aij=-aji
So favourable cases =73
Hence, required probability =7399
